newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-OLAZABAL RETURNS TO U.S. PGA TOUR THIS WEEK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-OLAZABAL RETURNS TO U.S. PGA TOUR THIS WEEK.

text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal returns to the U.S. PGA Tour after an injury absence of 19 months at this week's Freeport-McDermott Classic, buoyed by his emotional recent win on the European Tour.
"I'm very happy to be playing again, especially to come back to America and play in the Masters again," Olazabal said on the eve of the final tune-up event before the Masters.
"After not knowing if I would ever play golf again, it is a dream."
The 31-year-old Spaniard withdrew from golf in September of 1995 because pain in his feet, originally misdiognosed as rheumatoid arthritis, made it impossible for him to walk golf courses.
Despite the pain, his final two appearances in the United States -- at the 1995 International and World Series -- produced top 10 finishes.
When his condition was properly diagnosed last September as a herniated disc in his back, Olazabal was able to receive helpful treatment, and he began practicing again in January.

His game did not seem to suffer too much from the long layoff. Olazabal has played three times in Europe this year, finishing 12th in Dubai and fourth in Portugal before his emotional win at the Turespana Masters by two strokes 25 days after his first competitive round.
In 12 rounds of European golf, Olazabal was an impressive 41 strokes under par.
"Usually if I just take a few weeks off from golf it takes me longer than that to get my game back, so I have been very surprised at how well I've been able to play," Olazabal said.
Olazabal, who won his first major title at the 1994 Masters, is trying to be realistic about his chances at Augusta this year, since he still feels discomfort at the end of each round.

"We'll have to wait and see how it will be next week. There are a lot of hills and I will have to take it easy during the practice rounds. I'm just going to go there to enjoy the week as much as I can."

Countryman and European Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros is hoping Olazabal can continue to improve and qualify for the team to ensure that at least one Spaniard will compete on home turf this year at Valdarama.
Ballesteros has not been playing well this year, missing cuts on a regular basis, often by many strokes. He already withdrew from this week's event here, suffering from a severe head cold.
Olazabal said making the Ryder Cup team was not a high priority for him right now.
"I'm not even thinking about it at all," he said. "The Ryder Cup is not as important as feeling better and playing well again."
